messages:
Nina (AE): Heads-up: Meridian is looking to migrate from RivalAI to Redwood. Top concerns: JSON schema stability (their clients break on nulls/missing keys), predictable billing, and a security checklist. Quick sync in 1hr?
Omar (SE): I'll be there. Clarify: do they require exact text parity or schema parity?
Nina (AE): Quote from their eng: "Wire-compatible for 90% of endpoints; remaining diffs must be annotated in changelog." Sending small example they provided.
Nina (AE): ```
POST /v1/summarize
{ "text":"..." }
--- sometimes returns: { "title": null, "summary": "" }
```
Omar (SE): Typical mitigation: compat shim that enforces keys (null->""), optional deterministic sampling for parity runs, and schema validation step. I can prototype a tiny node proxy.
Rae (Solutions Eng): Agreed. I'll prepare a minimal shim repo + test harness that runs RivalAI vs Redwood and records diffs + token deltas. Need a 200-sample corpus from customer.
Priya (Customer Success): I'll collect 200 samples and the failing unit test. Also request their QPS patterns (peak/avg).
Lee (SRE): Perf note: per-request normalization adds ~10-30ms. If they have bursts we should propose Dedicated capacity. Also watch concurrency limits for private deployments.
Omar (SE): Draft acceptance thresholds to propose: schema pass rate >= 99%, median token increase <= 12%, 95th latency < 400ms on Dedicated. If they insist on exact parity, call out model checkpoint licensing as blocker.
legal-bot: Meridian requires SOC2, customer-managed KMS, EU data residency, and a signed DPA + SCCs. Legal needs completed questionnaire by EOD tomorrow.
Nina (AE): Owners: Omar = shim + parity POC, Rae = test harness, Lee = ops sizing, Priya = corpus & coordination, Legal = DPA/SLA. Next sync 24h after Omar's first parity run. :+1:
